summary: This paper presents a rigorous differential benchmark evaluating seven container image reference parsing libraries across Go, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, and Rust against the canonical distribution/reference Go package. Through 80 synthetic edge cases and 2,435 real-world image references from popular open-source repositories, the author reveals critical inconsistencies, including tag dropping when digests are present, missing localhost resolution, and permissive validation bypassing. The methodology and reproducibility instructions are exemplary.
strengths: Rigorous differential testing methodology comparing seven active third-party implementations against canonical distribution/reference behavior.

Comprehensive coverage of synthetic edge cases (Docker Hub defaults, host/port variations, IPv6 literals, compound tag-plus-digest strings, grammar limits) paired with a large real-world corpus of 2,435 image references across six prominent projects.
High reproducibility with exact compiler versions, package version locks, commit hashes, and detailed step-by-step reproduction instructions.
Detailed appendices explicitly listing the full verdict matrix and normalized output differences for every deviating parser.
weaknesses: The evaluation focuses exclusively on user-space library parsing and does not test how runtime daemons (such as dockerd or containerd) or specific registries handle the downstream invalid references accepted by permissive libraries like docker-py.
The paper notes container_image_dist_ref was excluded due to targeting non-normalizing Parse, but does not benchmark whether other ecosystem parsers (e.g., in Java or C#) exhibit similar divergences.
suggestions: Extend the analysis to end-to-end impact by testing whether daemons reject the malformed references passed by permissive libraries before network requests are dispatched.

Submit upstream bug reports or documentation pull requests to libraries with severe behavioral flaws, such as docker-parse-image misrouting localhost/app to Docker Hub and go-containerregistry discarding human-readable tags when digests are pinned.

claims.text: The OCI Distribution Specification defines the repository-name and tag grammars that a registry accepts, but not the short forms that people write. Those are defined by Docker's reference package, now maintained as distribution/reference, which Docker and containerd use.
go-containerregistry returns a digest reference and drops the tag; the image pulled is the same, because the digest decides, but a tool that reports or re-tags the image loses the tag.
claims.source: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/google/go-containerregistry/pkg/name#ParseReference (godoc notes: 'References that include both a tag and digest parse as Digest references')

claims.text: docker-py's parse_repository_tag splits off a tag or digest and auth.resolve_repository_name splits the registry from the repository.

novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Applies differential specification-conformance testing methodology to container image reference parsing across multilingual client libraries rather than HTTP server preconditions.
